summary.headline: Petronet LNG posted record Q2 FY27 PBT of INR1,659 crore (+53% YoY) helped by INR658 crore operational and commercial efficiency gains.
summary.overview: Petronet processed 231 TBTU of LNG in Q2, up 12% QoQ and 1% YoY, with Dahej at 216 TBTU. PBT rose to INR1,659 crore and PAT to INR1,235 crore, both up about 53% YoY, and H1 PBT and PAT grew 43% YoY. Management said the gains came from operational and commercial efficiencies, now reported as one combined figure. Qatar volumes remained curtailed by the Strait of Hormuz disruption, with only 6 of 28 scheduled July-September cargoes delivered. The board declared an interim dividend of INR7 per share.

financial_highlights.change: vs 192 TBTU QoQ and 211 TBTU YoY
vs 66% QoQ and 92% YoY; based on expanded 22.5 MTPA capacity
Q1 INR494 crore; Q2 FY26 INR41 crore
Petchem spend to 30 Sep about INR3,300 crore cumulative

segments.name: Regasification (Dahej and Kochi)
segments.commentary: Dahej ran at 73% utilisation on 22.5 MTPA expanded capacity, and regas service revenue was INR1,272 crore. Management declined to disclose the Dahej tariff and said it is the lowest in the country.

segments.name: Marketing / trading (incl. Qatar-linked volumes)
segments.commentary: Management now reports one combined efficiency figure of INR658 crore instead of separate trading and inventory gains. Qatar delivered 6 of 28 scheduled cargoes (July-September), and these were tolling-based, with management saying it does not take volume or price exposure.

segments.name: Petrochemical project (PDH-PP, Gopalpur)
segments.commentary: Cumulative spend about INR3,300 crore to 30 September, with H1 capex of INR1,626 crore. Physical progress is said to be on schedule, with an H2 capex uptick expected; useful life is 25 years and opex guidance is deferred about a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 aggregate capex about INR9,000 crore; FY28 at similar level; gradual trough from FY29.
Going forward, only one combined efficiency-gain figure will be guided, not trading and inventory gains separately.
Management expects the operational efficiency gains and lower throughput to offset each other across price cycles.
Kochi-Bangalore pipeline expected to connect to national grid within FY27, per management's conservative view (GAIL says December).
Interim dividend of INR7 per share declared; management says dividend per share will be maintained despite capex.
Depreciation run-rate from Q2 may be used, subject to quarterly guidance, while force majeure lease accounting continues.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex target about INR9,000 crore; H1 spend INR1,626 crore, so H2 must carry most of it.
Petchem cumulative spend about INR3,300 crore to 30 September; all major orders placed.
Dahej expanded capacity 22.5 MTPA versus 17.5 MTPA last year; the additional 5 MTPA expansion has no signed offtake or take-or-pay yet.
Three LNG charter vessels are under suspension during force majeure; Aseem charter runs to 2034 versus Qatar volumes to 2028.
LNG charter claims disclosed at INR625 crore in the note.
demand_pricing: India LNG imports: 25.3 MT in CY2025; 20.15 MT in first nine months of CY2026, which management says annualises to about 25 MT.
Demand gains cited in CGD, fertiliser and power; Qatar and UAE volumes replaced by US, Oman, Nigeria, Angola, Trinidad and Australia supply, mostly by capacity holders.
Management says October demand has been steady with no major decline; it disputed that spot LNG touched USD30/mmBtu in September.
Contract renewals with current offtakers (April 2028) are in ongoing discussion; management is hopeful of closure before the start date.
Qatar's new US long-term tie-ups start 2030-31, so no near-term uncommitted US volume is available to Petronet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of the INR625 crore LNG charter claim versus FY26 lease expense of INR690 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the claim includes charter charges and associated costs such as fuel, with counterclaims from Petronet also; the full detail is in the note.

qa_highlights.question: Can the three idle LNG vessels be sub-chartered?
qa_highlights.answer: The time charters are suspended, so lessors are free to use the vessels; management said it is talking to offtakers on usage and will not keep the vessel idle.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the revenue growth of about 30% QoQ versus about 11% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to the INR658 crore efficiency gains and Qatar-linked turnover, which is booked at higher value than the regas volume.

qa_highlights.question: How did efficiency gains behave in high versus low price periods?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said efficiencies are always present but are best monetised when prices are high; when prices fall, throughput rises and offsets the lower gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 5 MTPA Dahej expansion offtake status?
qa_highlights.answer: No offtake agreement or commitment has been signed for the additional 5 MTPA; tie-ups are expected quickly once the market normalises.

risks_watch: Qatar force majeure: only 6 of 28 July-September cargoes delivered; charter suspension and claims depend on its resolution.
Efficiency gains of INR658 crore are not split out and could reverse as spot LNG prices fall, which would lower reported earnings.
Contract renewal with existing offtakers in April 2028 is still ongoing.
Petchem project spend must rise sharply in H2 to meet the INR9,000 crore FY27 capex target; opex and returns not yet disclosed.
Depreciation is volatile under force majeure lease accounting; the Q2 run-rate may not hold.
summary.management_tone: Confident on results, calling it the best-ever Q2 and H1 for PBT and PAT, while management was evasive on efficiency-gain composition, tariff, and Qatar volume timing. Several answers were deflected to later guidance.
key_quotes: This has been our best ever second quarter as well as our best ever half year in terms of both PBT and PAT.
So in any way, either way, our capacity utilization of the plants remain the same as well as our margins are protected.
we don't bring any molecule on our own.

adds.what: Dahej expanded regas capacity to 22.5 MTPA (from 17.5 MTPA last year), already commissioned
Additional 5 MTPA Dahej expansion with no signed offtake or take-or-pay yet
PDH-PP petrochemical project at Gopalpur, physical progress on schedule, cumulative spend about INR3,300 crore to 30 Sep
Kochi-Bangalore pipeline connection to national grid expected within FY27 (management's conservative view)

growth.why: Management guided FY27 capex of about INR9,000 crore and FY28 at a similar level but gave no revenue growth number; Q2 throughput was up only 1% YoY with Qatar delivering 6 of 28 cargoes, while profit growth of 53% came from a INR658 crore efficiency figure rather than volume.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 PBT rose to INR1,659 crore (+53% YoY) on INR658 crore of efficiency gains (Q2 FY26 only INR41 crore), but management says these gains will fall as spot prices fall and may reverse, with no split disclosed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dahej expanded to 22.5 MTPA from 17.5 MTPA (+28.6%) is already commissioned; the 5 MTPA further expansion has no signed offtake, so it is not a firm near-term volume driver.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 throughput was up only 1% YoY at 231 TBTU and overall utilisation is 64% (vs 78% YoY), with Qatar delivering just 6 of 28 July-September cargoes; volume recovery depends on Qatar and demand, with October demand described as steady.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 64%, so no new plant is needed; the capex that matters (about INR9,000 crore FY27 target, only INR1,626 crore spent in H1) is already committed, and the 5 MTPA expansion is planned but has no offtake yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or volume guidance was given; management was evasive on efficiency-gain composition and Qatar timing, and profit strength is tied to one-off-like efficiency gains that could reverse.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Efficiency gains of INR658 crore could reverse as spot LNG prices fall, Qatar force majeure continues (6 of 28 cargoes), and the LNG charter claim is INR625 crore against FY26 lease expense of INR690 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PDH-PP petrochemical project at Gopalpur has about INR3,300 crore spent to 30 Sep with physical progress on schedule and all major orders placed, but opex guidance is deferred about a year.

rows.label: Kochi-Bangalore pipeline grid connection
rows.why: Management guides connection within FY27 (conservative view); GAIL says December, so this could come earlier than the FY27 window.

rows.label: Qatar force majeure resolution and charter claim
rows.why: Only 6 of 28 July-September cargoes were delivered; three idle charter vessels and a INR625 crore charter claim depend on how the force majeure is resolved.

rows.label: Contract renewal with existing offtakers (April 2028)
rows.why: Renewal talks with current offtakers are ongoing and management is hopeful of closure before the April 2028 start date, with no closure announced yet.

tone.note: Management was confident about the best-ever Q2 and H1 PBT/PAT and the capex plan, but was evasive on the composition of the INR658 crore efficiency gains, the Dahej tariff, and Qatar volume timing; analysts pushed on revenue growth versus volume and the sustainability of efficiency gains.
